question: What is the documentation difference between engineering judgment and an engineering study in the MUTCD definitions?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Based on the evidence provided, the key documentation distinction is that an engineering study must be documented — a deviation from a Standard provision is allowed only when the agency "fully documents, through an engineering study, the engineering basis for the deviation." Engineering judgment carries no stated documentation requirement in this evidence and is sufficient (alongside engineering study) only for deviations from Guidance provisions. Note that the formal definitions of "engineering study" and "engineering judgment" reside in Section 1C.02, which is not included in the evidence, so the precise definitional wording cannot be quoted here. Standards (mandatory): - "Where the content of this Manual requires a decision for implementation, such decisions shall be made by an engineer, or an individual under the supervision of an engineer, who has the appropriate levels of experience and expertise to make the traffic control device decision. Those decisions shall be made using engineering judgment or engineering study, as required by the MUTCD provision." - For Standard statements: "In limited, location-specific cases, the results of a documented engineering study (see Section 1D.03) might indicate a deviation from one or more requirements of a Standard provision to be appropriate." For Guidance statements: deviations are "allowed if engineering judgment or engineering study (see Section 1D.03) indicates the deviation to be appropriate." Citations: - Section 1A.04 Standard §2 (p.2) - Section 1C.01 Standard §1 (p.13) - Section 1D.03 Support §1 (p.32) - Section 1D.03 Support §2 (p.32) Supporting context (Support — informational only): - Section 1D.03 explains that in limited, site-specific cases where compliance with a Standard is impossible or impracticable, "the deviation is allowed, provided that the agency or official having jurisdiction fully documents, through an engineering study, the engineering basis for the deviation" — reinforcing that documentation is intrinsic to an engineering study when deviating from a Standard. - Section 1D.03 §1 notes that the actual definitions of professional engineer, engineering study, and engineering judgment are provided in Section 1C.02, which is not part of this evidence. - Section 4C.01 illustrates the documented character of an engineering study: agencies may install a signal where no warrants are met "only after conducting an engineering study that documents the rationale" for the decision.
gold_answer: Both involve evaluating pertinent information and applying engineering principles by a professional engineer or a person under such an engineer's supervision. Engineering judgment does not require documentation; an engineering study must be documented in writing.
